– the failing test (signature + snippet),

– likely-relevant recent bug reports,

If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The test case fails because it expects an IllegalArgumentException when both the input array and element to add are null (lines 228 and 229), but the current implementation of ArrayUtils.add(T[] array, T element) returns an Object[] array instead, leading to a ClassCastException instead of the expected exception.

Specifically, the add method determines the array component type (variable "type") as follows:
- If the input array is non-null, it uses the array's class type.
- Else if the element is non-null, it uses the element's class type.
- Else (if both are null), it uses Object.class as the component type.

Then it calls copyArrayGrow1(array, type) to create a new array bigger by one element.

In the copyArrayGrow1 method:
- If the input array is non-null, it grows the array by one element of the original component type.
- If the array is null (as in the test), it creates a new array of length 1 with the given component type (newArrayComponentType).

Since when both array and element are null, the type is set to Object.class, copyArrayGrow1 returns an Object[] array of length 1. The add method then tries to cast this Object[] to T[], which fails at runtime causing a ClassCastException.

The test expects an IllegalArgumentException to be thrown instead.

The root cause is that the add method does not handle the case of both parameters being null properly. It silently returns an Object[] even though from the type signature it should never allow that, causing an unexpected ClassCastException.

The recent bug report summary and description supports this analysis, explicitly noting the same issue where add(array, element) returns an Object[] when both args are null, leading to ClassCastException instead of error handling.

Hence, the bug is that ArrayUtils.add does not properly guard or throw when both parameters are null, leading to improper array type creation and ClassCastException at runtime.

No indications from other recent unrelated reports affect this conclusion.
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test `testLANG571()` expects an IllegalArgumentException when both the input array and the element to add are null. However, the `ArrayUtils.add(T[] array, T element)` method does not enforce this. Instead, it tries to infer the output array type by checking if the input array or element is non-null. If both are null, it defaults to using `Object.class` as the component type. Then, `copyArrayGrow1` creates a new array of this component type (which becomes `Object[]`). Afterwards, the method casts this `Object[]` back to `T[]` and returns it. This causes a ClassCastException at runtime because `Object[]` cannot be cast to a more specific array type `T[]`.

The test expects an exception but gets a ClassCastException due to this behavior. The root cause is a missing check and explicit exception throw when both parameters are null, causing the method to create an inappropriate array type instead of failing fast. The current bug report supports this analysis by pointing out the unexpected ClassCastException and undesirable returned type in this scenario.

Thus, the failure is caused by `ArrayUtils.add` returning an `Object[]` array when both input parameters are null, resulting in a ClassCastException instead of the expected IllegalArgumentException.

The relevant methods inspected are `ArrayUtils.add(T[], T)` and `ArrayUtils.copyArrayGrow1(Object, Class<?>)`.

Recommended fix: Add an explicit null check for the case when both array and element are null in `ArrayUtils.add` and throw IllegalArgumentException to match the test case expectations.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
